# PixelPointer Governance

[Português (Brasil)](GOVERNANCE.md) · **English** · [Español](GOVERNANCE.es.md)

## Responsibility

`@lzocateli` is the owner and sole maintainer authorized to accept scope, approve
contributions and merge changes into `main`. External contributions use forks
and PRs, as described in [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md). Third-party reviews
are advisory and do not replace the maintainer's decision.

## Main protection

Repository policies are a versioned contract in
[`repository-policy.json`](repository-policy.json), generated by
Altivy.Groundwork and applied by the maintainer with `groundwork github --sync`
(see [REPOSITORY-POLICY](REPOSITORY-POLICY.md)). `groundwork github` checks remote
configuration without changing it and returns `0` when it matches the contract.

| Ruleset | Controls | Exceptions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gw-main-integrity` | Blocks deletion and force-push, requires linear history and an up-to-date branch with the `Result` check | None, including for the owner |
| `gw-main-review` | Requires a PR and one approval, dismisses approvals after new commits, requires resolved conversations and squash merges | Administrator role, through PRs only |
| `gw-release-tags` | Restricts creation, update and deletion of `refs/tags/v*` | Only the `Altivy Release` GitHub App |

`Result` in [`ci.yml`](workflows/ci.yml) aggregates PR hygiene (Conventional
Commit title, actionlint and managed files), `Gitleaks / Full History` and
`Build, tests and Native AOT` for `linux-x64`, `win-x64` and `osx-arm64`; it fails
if any required job does not succeed. New jobs join `Result.needs` without
changing the ruleset.

[CODEOWNERS](CODEOWNERS) covers every file with `@lzocateli`. The file alone
does not block merges; enforcement depends on the active GitHub rulesets.

### Release tags and Environments

Only the `Altivy Release` GitHub App creates `v*` tags; even administrators do
not create them manually. Stable `vX.Y.Z` tags still originate from merging
the release-please Release PR. Before publication, `gw-release.yml` verifies
the version and ancestry of `origin/main`.

On 2026-10-31, the maintainer authorized a public-preview exception:
`workflow_dispatch` of `publish.yml` on `main` may create `vX.Y.Z-preview.N`
using the same App, after build, tests and approval in the `release` Environment.
The job checks the commit, checksums and remote digests and publishes as
Pre-release, without `Latest`, Homebrew, winget or deploy. PRs still receive
no secrets and do not publish previews. This exception does not permit manual
tag creation, update or deletion; `gw-release-tags` remains unchanged.
Details and recovery: [release process](../docs/en/release.md#required-preview).

The `release` Environment requires approval by `@lzocateli` to upload assets
to the draft release and again to update the Homebrew tap in `post-release.yml`
(`HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` exists only there). `winget` requires approval by
`@lzocateli` for automatic and manual submissions and allows only `main` and
`v*` references. `prevent_self_review` is disabled so the sole maintainer can
consciously approve a run they started. GitHub also allows administrative
bypass (`can_admins_bypass=true`), currently limited to the same maintainer.
PRs and validations without `submit=true` do not run the submission job or
access `WINGET_CREATE_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

### Third-party PRs

1. The maintainer authorizes external contributors' workflow runs after
   inspecting their contents; permission to run CI is not PR approval.
2. CI must pass and conversations must be resolved.
3. The maintainer reviews and records approval before merging.
4. Only the maintainer can perform the merge.

### Maintainer-authored PRs

GitHub does not allow an `Approve` review on one's own PR. The maintainer may
merge their PR using the review exception in `gw-main-review`, recording the
decision and evidence in the PR. The exception does not waive `Result`, branch
freshness or `gw-main-integrity`; it does not allow direct push, force-push
or deletion.

Technically, it also permits merging a third-party PR without a formal review;
project policy requires recording approval in that case. It is neither formal
self-approval nor an automatic author check.

### Guarantee limits

The exception is tied to `RepositoryRole: Admin` (ID `5`), not an individual
user. The repository was created on 2026-10-30 from F0, the feasibility spike
([report](../docs/f0-relatorio.md)). Subsequent deliveries follow Issue, phase
of the [plan](../docs/plano-implementacao.md), branch and PR.

Publication and `release` Environment approval are separate from merging
ordinary PRs: only the Release PR merge starts a stable release; public previews
follow the approved exception above. See the [release process](../docs/en/release.md).

## Verification and recovery

Drift signals include accepted direct pushes, third-party merges, missing
checks or expanded administrative exceptions. From a clone root, with `gh`
authenticated as the owner, these commands are read-only:

```bash
groundwork github
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/rulesets
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/rules/branches/main
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/rules/tags/v0.0.0
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/environments/winget
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/environments/winget/deployment-branch-policies
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/collaborators
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/private-vulnerability-reporting
gh api repos/lzocateli/PixelPointer/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval
```

Expected: `groundwork github` exits `0`; both branch `gw-*` rulesets are active
on `refs/heads/main` (integrity without bypass, review with administrative PR-only
bypass); `Result` is tied to GitHub Actions; only the owner is an administrator;
`gw-release-tags` has App-only bypass; `winget` requires maintainer approval and
`main`/`v*` references; private reports are enabled; workflows use
`all_external_contributors` approval.

If configuration drifts, suspend merges and publication, remove unauthorized
access, restore rules in **Settings > Rules > Rulesets** and repeat the checks.
For suspected compromise, revoke affected tokens and sessions and contact the
owner; vulnerabilities follow the security policy. Do not disable rules to
bypass broken CI: fix the workflow or change the check name through an explicit,
traceable decision.
